questions.q: What is the first question worth asking when you notice a fault in the car?
options: How long the repair will take at the garage
What exactly is happening, when it happens, and which system is involved
questions.explain: The method starts with three questions in order: what exactly is happening, when it happens, and which system in the car is involved. They narrow down the suspects before you turn to the matching diagnosis tree.

questions.q: What does the “stop now” severity level mean in this chapter's diagnosis trees?
options: The car will fail its annual roadworthiness test
There is immediate danger — stop in a safe place and do not keep driving
You can keep driving carefully to the garage
You need to reach a garage within a week
questions.explain: “Stop now” marks immediate danger — for example extreme engine heat, smoke or brake failure — where you do not keep going, and stop in a safe place instead.

questions.q: Which of the following is safe and normal for a driver to check themselves, without special tools?
options: Connecting a scan tool to the car
Fluid levels when the engine is cold, and tyre air pressure
questions.explain: Checking fluid levels, air pressure, warning lights and stains is safe and simple to do yourself. Taking parts apart, replacing pads, and computerised diagnosis belong to the garage.

questions.q: A thin, steady squeal heard on every braking usually points to what?
questions.explain: A small metal strip in the pad produces a deliberate squeal once the pad nears its minimum thickness — a reminder to replace it soon.

questions.q: A rhythmic metallic knock whose speed rises with engine RPM points mainly to what?
options: A suspected internal engine problem, needing an immediate check
questions.explain: A knock whose speed is tied to engine RPM hints at an internal mechanical engine fault — a serious condition that needs stopping and an immediate check, not continuing to drive.

questions.q: A hum that changes with road speed (not with engine RPM), and gets stronger when turning in one direction, usually points to what?
questions.explain: A hum linked to road speed, that gets stronger when turning in one direction, is a classic sign of a worn wheel bearing.

questions.q: A knock heard only when turning sharply, such as pulling into a parking space, usually points to what?
questions.explain: A rhythmic knock only in a sharp turn usually points to a worn CV joint, mainly in front-wheel-drive cars.

questions.q: Thin white vapour from the exhaust on a cold morning, which disappears after a minute's driving, is usually —
options: A sign of a damaged head gasket
questions.explain: Thin vapour that disappears quickly on a cold morning is water condensed in the exhaust pipe — a normal occurrence in any car, not real smoke.

questions.q: Thick white exhaust smoke that continues and sweetens the air usually points to what?
options: Coolant burning in the combustion chambers
questions.explain: Thick white smoke that continues, and doesn't disappear after a minute, points to coolant getting into the combustion chambers — usually a damaged cylinder head gasket.

questions.q: Bluish exhaust smoke, mainly noticeable on acceleration, usually points to what?
questions.explain: Bluish smoke, mainly on acceleration, points to engine oil burning in the combustion chambers — usually worn piston rings or valve seals.

questions.q: You smell a strong fuel smell inside the car. What is the right thing to do?
options: Don't start the engine, move away from the car, and don't light a flame near it
Turn on the air conditioning to clear the smell
Open a window and carry on as normal
Keep driving slowly until you get home
questions.explain: A strong fuel smell is a sign of a leak and a real fire risk. Don't start the engine, move away from the car, and don't light a flame or a cigarette near it.

questions.q: You find a clear fluid stain under the middle of the car, on a hot day, after driving with the air conditioning on. What is it likely to be?
options: Water from AC condensation — a normal occurrence
questions.explain: Clear fluid collecting under the middle of the car on a hot day, after driving with the air conditioning on, is ordinary water from AC condensation — no action is needed.

questions.q: A green, watery fluid stain under the front of the car, near the radiator — what is this likely to be?
questions.explain: A green, orange or pink, watery stain near the radiator is leaking coolant — from a pipe, the radiator, or the water pump.

questions.q: You see a clear-to-yellowish, oily fluid stain near one of the wheels. What is the right thing to do?
options: Add engine oil and carry on
Keep driving and check it at the next service
Don't drive the car, as this is likely leaking brake fluid
Inflate the tyre on that wheel
questions.explain: A clear-to-yellowish, oily stain near a wheel is usually brake fluid. The brake system is hydraulic and sealed, so you don't drive with a leak like this.

questions.q: Vibration in the steering wheel that appears only at a certain speed, and disappears when you speed up or slow down from it, usually points to what?
questions.explain: Vibration tied to a certain speed, which disappears outside that range, is almost always a sign of an unbalanced wheel, needing rebalancing at a tyre garage.

questions.q: You feel vibration or pulsing in the brake pedal, mainly when braking from high speed. What does this usually point to?
options: A brake disc that isn't an even thickness
questions.explain: Pulsing in the brake pedal when braking from high speed almost always points to a brake disc that has warped or worn unevenly.

questions.q: The car consistently pulls to one side, even without braking, on a straight, level road. What do you check first?
questions.explain: A difference in tyre air pressure is the most common cause of pulling to one side, and also the cheapest to fix — always check it first.

questions.q: Both the headlights are weak and the dashboard lights don't come on. The main suspect is —
options: A blown fuse in one circuit
A flat battery or loose terminals
questions.explain: When everything is weak or off, including the dashboard lights, the main suspect is a flat battery, or corroded or loose terminals.

questions.q: Only one electric window has stopped working, while everything else is fine. What do you check first?
questions.explain: When a single device stops working and everything else is fine, the first suspect is a blown fuse in that circuit — check it before anything else.

questions.q: The headlights dim when you switch on the air conditioning, and a battery warning light comes on while driving. What is the main suspect?
options: A fault in the charging system (alternator)
questions.explain: Headlights that dim under load, and a battery warning light that comes on while driving, point to a weak alternator or its drive belt — the car is running on what's left in the battery.

questions.q: You smell a burning plastic smell, and see a little smoke from the dashboard. What is the right thing to do?
options: Carry on to the nearest garage
Turn on the air conditioning to clear the smoke
Stop immediately, switch off the engine and the electrics, and get out of the car
Keep driving with the windows open
questions.explain: Smoke and a burning smell from the dashboard are a sign of a dangerous electrical fault. Stop immediately, switch off the engine and the electrics, and get out of the car with all the passengers.
